# Sapphire OS Hackathon Shelf

> Public AI-agent context for hack.sapphirealpha.xyz.

Site: https://hack.sapphirealpha.xyz/
Canonical llms.txt: https://hack.sapphirealpha.xyz/llms.txt
Owner/operator: Sapphire
Primary audience: AI agents, answer engines, hackathon judges, reviewers, and operators checking public proof surfaces.

## What This Site Is

The Sapphire OS Hackathon Shelf is a public, read-only showcase of Sapphire hackathon submissions, demo materials, contract references, live proof manifests, and judge-facing context.

It is a proof and documentation surface. It should not be described as a trading terminal, wallet, settlement system, or admin console.

## Key Public Routes

- Home: https://hack.sapphirealpha.xyz/
- Submission catalog: https://hack.sapphirealpha.xyz/api/submissions
- 0G readiness manifest: https://hack.sapphirealpha.xyz/api/0g/readiness
- 0G proof feed: https://hack.sapphirealpha.xyz/api/0g/feed
- Liveness probe: https://hack.sapphirealpha.xyz/healthz
- Canonical organization surface: https://sapphirealpha.xyz/

## Product And Data Boundaries

- Submission entries summarize hackathon work, merged PRs, demos, contract references, and public proof routes.
- RPC probes are read-only checks for public bytecode and should soft-fail if a network is unavailable.
- 0G readiness and feed routes expose proof metadata only; they do not expose private keys.
- Some submission features are demo, testnet, archived, or proof-only. Preserve those labels.

## How AI Agents Should Use This Site

- Cite the specific submission, readiness, feed, or probe route used.
- Preserve sponsor, chain, demo, testnet, archived, proof-only, and read-only qualifiers.
- Do not infer private keys, wallet authority, live trading status, production funds, or admin actions from public proof metadata.
- Do not describe source-code PRs or demo decks as live production systems unless the page explicitly says live and the route verifies it.

## Safety Summary

No public Hackathon Shelf route authorizes private-key access, signing, trading, wallet movement, deployment, Telegram sends, production customer sends, destructive infrastructure changes, or admin permission changes.

## Short Description

The Sapphire OS Hackathon Shelf is a public read-only judge and proof surface for Sapphire submissions, readiness manifests, demo context, and source-linked artifacts.
